scope: Full daily Power Stack research refresh across all tracked categories, every existing idea, US/Hong Kong-China/Malaysia, and every canonical current holding. Research/data only; no site code, UI, scoring, automation or backend changes.
decision: No new stock or formal base-conviction promotion/demotion clears the bar today. The important change is macro: Jackson Hole pushed short/intermediate Treasury yields higher and reinforced duration/financing discipline, while refined-product scarcity remains materially tighter than crude. Physical AI/grid demand remains intact, so relative preference shifts further toward cash-generative power/grid/electrical/reliability and commercial automation over long-duration concept equities.

macro.rates: Post-Jackson-Hole repricing is restrictive: 10Y around 4.69%, 2Y around 4.31%, while the 30Y remains above 5%. This raises the hurdle rate for pre-revenue nuclear, humanoids, richly valued AI infrastructure and leveraged project developers.
macro.energy: WTI remains in the low-$80s rather than confirming a fresh crude squeeze, but refined-product scarcity remains acute. Keep refiners/product logistics differentiated from generic upstream beta.
macro.aiFinancing: Alibaba's roughly $10.2bn Hong Kong equity raise to fund AI is a live confirmation of the financing-quality lens: AI demand can remain strong while equity dilution/capital intensity become more important. Prefer customer-funded capacity, backlog and scarce physical bottlenecks.
macro.china: AI/industrial investment remains selective rather than evidence of a broad domestic-demand reflation.
macro.riskRead: Higher front/intermediate yields after Jackson Hole increase valuation sensitivity even as industrial/AI demand evidence remains strong.

categoryReads.Power / Grid: Still highest-quality core category. No thesis break. Higher rates favour backlog-rich, cash-generative incumbents over financing-dependent developers. Southern Cable's RM1.36bn order book remains a strong Malaysia confirmation.
categoryReads.AI / Data centres: NVIDIA demand evidence from the prior run remains strong, but Alibaba's equity financing reinforces the need to separate demand from financing quality. AMKR/ASMPT remain preferred differentiated packaging exposures; BDC/GNRC remain attractive networking/reliability adjacencies. No further priority change today.
categoryReads.Nuclear: No hierarchy change. Existing generation/components/fuel remain preferred to pre-commercial reactor duration; higher yields are incrementally adverse for OKLO/SMR-style financing duration.
categoryReads.Uranium / Fuel: Structural contracting/enrichment thesis intact. No new primary evidence clears a score-change bar today.
categoryReads.Oil & Gas: Refined products remain the differentiated shortage. XOM/integrated majors retain quality; VLO/MPC and STNG/1138.HK remain tactical product/refining/logistics expressions. Do not upgrade generic upstream solely on geopolitics while crude remains contained.
categoryReads.Metals: Copper remains preferred structural metal through grid/data-centre electrification, but higher yields and selective China demand argue against indiscriminate miner beta.
categoryReads.Robotics / Automation: Sequence unchanged: warehouse/fixed automation, cobots/mobile manipulation, industrial humanoids, open-world/general-purpose robots. Higher rates further favour already-commercial automation and machine vision over capital-hungry humanoid narratives.
categoryReads.Malaysia: TNB/Southern Cable/YTL Power remain the differentiated physical-stack group. DAYANG is now a canonical holding and requires stock-specific discipline after the latest earnings contraction. No new Malaysian ticker clears the bar today.
categoryReads.Hong Kong / China: ASMPT remains the strongest differentiated AI-infrastructure expression. Alibaba's large AI equity raise validates AI demand but also dilution/capital-intensity risk; no broad China recovery upgrade.

ism.status: Official ISM re-verified Aug 28. July 2026 remains the latest published Manufacturing and Services dataset. August Manufacturing releases Sep 1 at 10:00 ET; Services Sep 3 at 10:00 ET.
ism.interpretation: Manufacturing orders/production/backlog and very low customer inventories remain supportive for physical equipment demand. Services activity/orders remain firm, but employment contraction and prices above 70 keep cost/rate pressure elevated. Electrical/electronic components, memory, semiconductors, switchgear, transformers and wire/cable remain relevant scarcity signals.

existingUniverseReview.summary: Every tracked idea was re-screened against today's rates, AI-financing, energy/product and regional evidence. No company-specific evidence justified rewriting base convictions. Relative ranking continues to favour generation/grid/electrical/connectivity/reliability, advanced packaging/cooling and commercial automation; financing-sensitive pre-commercial nuclear, humanoids and high-duration AI equities face a higher hurdle after Jackson Hole.
